newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan reports Moslem preachers' visits to China.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan reports Moslem preachers' visits to China.

text.p: Pakistan said on Thursday that a Moslem preaching group based here had made visits to China's troubled northwestern Xinjiang region in the past but had not interfered in China's internal affairs.

A Foreign Ministry spokesman also denied a newspaper report that China had protested to Pakistan about the alleged shipment of religious literature by the Tableeghi Jamaat group to incite unrest in Xinjiang, which borders northern Pakistan.

"We are studying the situation and watching the situation," he told reporters when asked about last week's anti-Chinese riots in Xinjiang by members of the Moslem Uighur minority. At least nine people were killed and nearly 200 injured.

"But the allegation as regards Pakistan and the Tableeghi Jamaat, they are incorrect," he said. "There had been some visits of the Tableeghi Jamaat in the past, but they were peaceful and never involved in any political activity that interfered with the internal affairs of China."
He did not specify when these visits occurred.
The spokesman also said China had not complained to Pakistan about the Tableeghi Jamaat. "The Chinese government has not protested to Pakistan," he said.
He said Sino-Pakistan relations were based on strict adherence to non-interference in each other's internal affairs.

Chinese officials have accused unidentified "hostile foreign forces" of fomenting the unrest in Yining city, 50 km (30 miles) from the border with Kazakhstan, where many exiled Uighur separatists live.

Xinjiang authorities last year stepped up a crackdown on separatists and underground religious activity after clashes, bombings and assassination attempts on officials and Moslem leaders regarded as pro-Beijing.
